 "content": "---
name: arc-frame-mask-recolor
description: Use when an ARC grid has repeated framed panels with zero-cell silhouettes and separate colored objects. Match each silhouette to an object and recolor the mask.
---

# ARC framed-mask recoloring

Use this when the input has a column of repeated rectangular panels on one side and a set of colored shapes on the other, often separated by all-background rows/columns.

## Rule

The repeated panel blocks contain a constant frame/background color (for example 8) with zero-valued cells inside that trace silhouettes. The separate colored objects are the color-coded versions of those silhouettes. For each panel, find the distinct object with the same shape, then replace the zero cells of that panel's silhouette with that object's color. Keep all frame/background cells unchanged. Output only the transformed panel area, excluding the reference objects and any separating blank columns.

The objects may appear in a different order than the panels. Match by silhouette, not by order or color assumptions. Silhouettes can be translated within their panels; compare shape up to translation. Preserve each mask's exact orientation and cell pattern.

## Procedure

1. Identify the framed-panel region and its constant color; locate separators between panels.
2. Extract each panel's zero-cell pattern, excluding the constant frame.
3. Extract each reference object's occupied cells and color from the other region.
4. Normalize each shape's coordinates by subtracting its minimum row and column. Compare normalized cell sets (same orientation; only translation is irrelevant).
5. For each panel, recolor its zero mask with the color of its matching reference object. Leave nonzero cells as-is.
6. Return the panel region in the original row order and width, retaining separator/frame rows and omitting the reference-object area.
7. Verify dimensions and confirm every mask received a unique silhouette match.

## Learned example / pitfall

In one instance, a 17x10 input consisted of a 5-column-wide, 8-framed panel stack on the left and four colored silhouettes on the right. The correct answer was the left 17x5 region with its zeros recolored to match the corresponding right-side silhouettes. Initial failure came from assigning colors by object order; the correct mapping is by exact shape. A later correction to the bottom panel likewise depended on matching its mask's silhouette rather than its apparent row sequence.

A separate demonstration used a 1-framed 10x6 panel stack and objects to the right. The output preserved the 6-column panel region and replaced the zero masks with the matching object colors, even though the reference objects were not in panel order. This confirms both order-independent shape matching and output cropping to the panel region.",
